_heapMB_note: 2026-08-26 SOLVED. The old note (kept below) said this gate read 307-415 MB run to run on identical worlds, listed five ruled-out causes, and set 460 above the observed maximum so it would stop refusing deploys at random. The cause was THE SETTLE BEFORE SAMPLING. Bisected: the same script, same page, one variable changed -- 2500ms of settle reads 415 MB and calls it settled, 12000ms reads 347-368, 20000ms reads 242. The world is still allocating after __ready, gc() cannot reclaim what is still live, and the stability test (three readings agreeing within 1%) passes on a quiet stretch INSIDE a climb -- the fourth time this project has measured a climb and called it a plateau. It is the settle that matters, not the sampling window: 12s of settle still reads 368 even when sampled across 30s. livecheck waits 20s now and reads 242 / 242 / 242 across three consecutive runs. Budget 460 -> 300, which is 24% of headroom over an exactly reproducible number. OLD NOTE, for the history: 2026-08-06 FINAL: the LIVE island settles at 192 MB (192/192/192, twice), UNDER the ~206MB iOS ceiling. THIS GATE, however, reads 307-415 MB and varies run to run on worlds whose triangle and draw counts are identical. FIVE causes have been tested and RULED OUT: uncollected garbage (gc is forced), the legacy ?streamall all-districts path (now loads the real district), the --use-gl=angle GPU flag (an independent probe with it reads a stable 228), sampling too early (a 2.5s settle changed nothing), and mobile emulation (isMobile/hasTouch changed nothing). An independent probe with the SAME url, flags, context and settle reads 228 stably while this file reads 347-415, so the difference is something else in livecheck itself and is NOT yet found. 460 sits above the observed maximum so the gate stops refusing deploys at random; it is deliberately loose and should be tightened to about 260 once the discrepancy is understood.
_hot_note: 2026-08-23. The four budgets above are read at the ARRIVAL POINT and nowhere else, which is how the island came to run 1,630 draws at Tanjong Beach Walk while the deploy passed the same build at 237. data/hotviews.mjs now visits the five heaviest views the coverage sweep finds, on the GAME path with touch forced (TILE is 240 on touch, 110 on desktop). Measured after the consolidate.js flatten + coarse-group work: worst 682 draws / 1642k tris. Budgets set just above that. These are necessarily looser than the spawn budgets and must stay separate from them; do not merge the two. 2026-08-31: 1750 -> 1600. qtrees.js stopped drawing the canopy BEHIND the camera (the bearing note in that file) and the worst view fell 1716k -> 1488k triangles with 46 of 46 goldens at 0.000% and data/spincheck's 28 spun frames identical. Ratcheted so the win cannot be spent silently: 1600 still leaves 112k of headroom, more than three times the 34k the old ceiling left over the old number.
_bootMs_note: 2026-08-26: 30000 -> 26000, because the number being budgeted was not boot. `bootMs` was computed AFTER the heap settle and the whole gc sampling loop, so it reported boot PLUS the measurement -- the published 'boot 26.8s' was about 19s of boot and 8s of stopwatch. Found by lengthening the settle and watching the reported boot jump to 38s on a world whose boot had not changed. Measured at the moment __ready flips it is 17.2 / 17.2 / 17.3 s across three runs. 26000 leaves 50% headroom, which this file still needs: boot is genuinely load-sensitive (see the three-run median rule).
